title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Previous 10% price increase (2025-07-28) had no negative impact (x1.29). No data on 6.2% increase. Recent weeks at $12.03 show 13 and 24 units vs baseline 18.7—mixed. The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is x1.4, but this is a price hike, not a discount. A 6.2% increase likely reduces demand

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. A price increase of 6.2% to $12.03 from $11.33 is a known demand-lowering driver. Recent weeks show no promotion, but a prior 30% off in 2024 lifted sales to x2.47 vs baseline—however, this was a deep discount. The current 6.2% increase is not a promotion, so it should suppress demand. Past price changes show no direct data, but a 10% price increase (2025-07-28) had minimal effect (x1.29). The recent 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks at $12.03 saw 13 and 24 units—vs baseline 18.7, implying a slight lift despite price, possibly due to seasonality. But the 2026-10-05 week was after a promotion (2026-09-28), so it’s not clean. No event or promotion in the target week. The classical model suggests no uplift, and evidence is thin. Price increase likely suppresses demand, but effect is uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0. No other drivers.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 4.5 - 37.5 | 10%-90%: 8.2 - 33.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
